Thanks Marissa — got it. I reviewed the draft runbook and sketched an orchestration lane for the cutover. High level plan below; I'll attach a trimmed runbook they can circulate to SOC.

Planned cutover lane (brief):
- Pre-cutover (T-48 to T-1 hours): provisioning check, test users created, SCIM dry-run to ensure delta mapping, export current allowlist.
- Cutover window (proposed): 2026-11-30 from 22:00 - 23:00 UTC (1 hour) — prefer late-night in US for minimal user impact.
  - Step 1 (00-10m): disable staging SAML endpoint (redirect).
  - Step 2 (10-25m): switch prod metadata for SAML and validate assertion attributes (email, sub, groups).
  - Step 3 (25-40m): enable SCIM delta provisioning on a 5m cadence for first 30m; monitor for errors.
  - Step 4 (40-50m): apply IP allowlist from pacehealth-ip-allowlist.csv at their firewall edge and our ingress.
  - Step 5 (50-60m): smoke tests with 6 pre-provisioned test users and two canary tenants.
- Post-cutover (T+1 to T+72 hours): elevated monitoring, token/session invalidation window, delivery of audit artifacts (SAML logs, SCIM events, request traces).

Rollback triggers: failed SCIM sync (>5% error rate), failed SAML auth validation, spike in 5xx errors from inference plane. Rollback steps are the inverse of cutover with immediate re-enable of previous metadata and allowlist.

I'll attach: trimmed runbook (for SOC), IP allowlist CSV, and a short naming guideline for service accounts. Please review and flag any missing items.

Questions for PaceHealth (Samira/Alan):
1) Can you confirm if the firewall change requires a maintenance ticket on your side, and if so, what's the SLA for that change?
2) Do you have a SOC contact for real-time coordination during cutover (phone bridge)?

Attaching: pacehealth-ip-allowlist.csv, service-accounts-naming-guidelines.md, pacehealth-cutover-runbook-v1.pdf

-Jordan

Samira — noted. On SCIM: a couple of specifics to call out in the trimmed runbook so you can sign off quickly:

- Attribute mapping: our SCIM mapping will provision user.email -> userName and user.externalId -> externalId if present. Groups are mapped to an enterprise_groups array. We'll include a sample payload in the runbook.
- Delta sync cadence: default to 5m for first hour, then 15m for T+24h if no errors.
- Pagination & rate limits: we'll honor up to 120 req/min and exponential backoff on 429s; if your org is large, we can enable batched SCIM (bulk) for initial full sync.
- Test users: please create 6 test accounts with these attributes: two admins, two clinicians, two read-only users. Include one user with multi-group membership to validate group claims in SAML.

I'll add a short example SAML AttributeStatement block in the runbook (email, sub, groups, role). Jordan — I'll paste that in the trimmed PDF and also drop the JSON sample in Drive.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Identity Engineer | Redwood Inference

Couple of operational notes from the infra side:

- Service accounts: we recommend the following naming convention: rhw-pace-<purpose>-svc (e.g., rhw-pace-scim-proxy-svc). Least privilege roles will be scoped to: scim:write (provisioning), sso:verify (assertion logs), logs:read (audit export).
- Audit artifacts we'll provide post-cutover: SAML assertion logs (timestamp, issuer, subject, outcome), SCIM event log (create/update/delete, result code), request traces across the inference gateway (request id, latency, upstream id). We'll hand these off as zipped JSON lines for your SOC.
- IP allowlist: attached is our recommended ingress set. If PaceHealth requires a temporary bypass for their VPN IPs, note that this creates a short-lived elevated-access vector — log emission will be elevated.

I'll be on the bridge during cutover and can roll back ingress rules within 3-5 minutes if needed.
